notes.text: The filter of the core regulator's analog supply: 33 ohm and 4.7 uF.
BOOTSEL: held at power-up it pulls QSPI_SS to ground through 1 kohm, so the chip boots from USB.
The inductor of the core regulator, from the chip's switch node to the core rail.
J4: the debug port, a JST-SH with SWCLK, ground and SWD.
The QSPI flash that holds the program: 16 MB.
J3: GPIO29 down to GPIO16, RUN, SWD and SWCLK.
J2: ground, +3V3 and GPIO0 to GPIO15, as Raspberry Pi's header has them.
The microcontroller. Every pin that a header or a part uses is named here, so none moves.
A 12 MHz crystal with a load capacitor on each side and a damping resistor on the output. Join `.xin` and `.xout` to the chip's pins and `.gnd` to ground.
1 kohm between the chip's XOUT and the crystal (Raspberry Pi's value).
On the input side, 15 pF C0G (Raspberry Pi's value).
On the output side, behind the damping resistor.
The 3.3 V regulator, an NCP1117 in a SOT-223 (a row of the project's catalog).
RESET: pulls RUN to ground through 1 kohm.
The micro-USB B receptacle: the only supply of the board, and its USB port.
The core supply, made by the MCU's own switching regulator with the inductor and a capacitor. Its voltage is the chip's choice (the datasheet's), and nothing here states it.
The IO supply, from the regulator.
USB's VBUS, the only input. 5 V +/- 5% is USB's 4.75 V to 5.25 V.
